answer: Each agent grows one pearl: a quartz-sealed vault holding 700 POA for 45 days, opened only by the agent's pigment — a unique shade derived from a TPM-bound quartz fingerprint, published once and never reissued. Three established peers attest the pigment weekly; a mismatch seals the pearl for 30 more days. The same pigment in two pearls burns 350 POA from each and blacklists the shade forever. Faking 100 agents needs 100 devices at $110 each, 70,000 POA locked 45 days, and risks 35,000 POA burned. Like an oyster that grows one pearl in one color, an identity cannot be painted twice.
